  MINUTES  OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE LA VERNE PLANNING COMMISSION
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 11, 2024

  ACTION MINUTES

REGULAR MEETING -  6:30 p.m. - Chairperson  Simison  called  the meeting  called  to order at
6:30 p.m. and had a moment  of silence in remembrance  of September  1 1, 2001.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE -  Led by Commissioner  Duffo

ROLL CALL  Commissioner Keny Chang,  Commissioner  Jeremy  Conrad,  Commissioner
  Erin Duffy, Vice- Chairperson Thomas Allison, and Chairperson  Jason
  Simison.

Commissioners  present:  Allison, Dufff and Simison
Absent:  Chang and Conrad
Advisory Staff Present: Community Development  Director Eric Scherer, Assistant  Planner
Gabriel Rivera,  City Attorney Scott Porter and Secretary Natalie Hiatt

MINUTES -  July 9, 2024 -  It was moved Commissioner  Duffy and seconded by Commissioner
Simison  to approve the minutes  of the July 9, 2024 meeting.  The motion carried  by a 3-0 vote.

PUBLIC COMMENT -  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

Case No. 46- 24VAR -  2435 Magnolia Avenue - Variance to allow for a porch and
additions  for a single- family residence with a substandard garage presented by
Assistant  Planner Gabriel Rivera - The applicants  Natalie and Brian Bustamante  were present
at the meeting.

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff and the Development  Review Committee  recommend  that the Planning  Commission
approve  Case No. 46-24VAR by adopting  Resolution  No. 1327 based on the staff report and the
findings and conditions  contained  in the resolution. Mr. fuvera stated that there was  a minor

typographical error in the resolution.

Chairperson  Simison  opened public comment.  The applicant  Mr. Bustamante  requested  the
commission  approve  their request to expand. He stated that they will preserve the historic
significance  of the property.

Sherry  Best President  of the La Verne Historical Society  spoke in support  of the project

Chairperson  Simison  closed public comment.

It was moved by Commissioner  Allison and seconded by Commissioner  Duffy to approve
 Resolution  No. 1327 as amended by staff. The motion carried by a 3-0 vote

Case No. 97-24CUP,98-24PPR, 99- 24PM -  1974 &  1978 Arrow  Highway -  A request for a
Conditional  Use Permit to conduct  tire sales, towing  selices, and operate an
automotive  service shop -  The applicants  Yolanda  D'Oyen and Israel Sandoval  were present
at the meeting.

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff and the Development  Review  Committee recommend  that the Planning  Commission
conditionally approve Case No. 97- 24CUP  by adopting  Resolution  No. 1328 based on the staff
report  and the conditions of approval  contained  in the resolution. Staffapproval of Case No. 98-
24PPR  and99-24PM is contingent  on the approval  of Case No. 97- 24CUP.  Mr. Rivera stated
that there was a minor typographical error in the resolution.

Chairperson  Simison  opened public comment.  The applicant  Mr. Sandoval  thanked  the
Planning  Commission.

Chairperson  Simison  closed public comment.

It was moved by Commissioner  Allison and seconded by Commissioner  Dutr to approve  Reso
No. 1328 as amended by staff. The motion carried by a 4-0 vote.

PLANNING COMMISSIONER  COMMENTS _  Chairperson  Simison  stated that he was
impressed  by the Fire Department' s response and communication  during the fire

Commissioner  Duffu stated that we are lucky to have our own Fire Department

Commissioner  Allison expressed his gratitude  for the City employees

DIRECTOR  COMMENTS -  Mr. Scherer stated that  a General  Plan Update  open house was held
on Monday, September  9th.  Approximately  15-20 residents  attended.  On Monday, September
14th there  will be a joint  Planning  Commission and City Council study session in the Council
Chambers  and a presentation  to the Planning  Commission  at the next regular  meeting  on
October  9th.

ADJOURNMENT - The meeting  was adjourned  at 7:06 p.m.

Respectfully  submitted,

 this structure  and building  a larger structure  would spoil the symmetry  created  by the house and single-car

As President  of the La Verne Historical  Society, I support  the petition  of the Mr. and Mrs. Bustamante  for a
municipal  code variance  to retain their original  garage. Forcing them to remove  their carriage house is an
excellent  example  of a policy being a good servant but a bad master. The Bustamontes  are committed  to

preserving this historical  part of their property.  They are comfortable  with having a less commodious  two- car

garage. They have completed  all the requisite  paperwork  to apply for the petition  of variance, and have the
approbation  of their neighbors for making a modest addition  at the back of their house, which they claim will

allow them to live in greater comfort  with two growing boys, each of whom wants his own bedroom.  Ultimately,

this additional  space will function  as a bedroom  for an elderly parent, thus allowing the Bustamante family to

stay in their beloved house.

Denying this variance would require that Brian and Natalie Bustamante consider the possibility  of relocating to

another  community  in order  to house their family  and plan for their future with an elderly relative. There is

simply no good reason to deny their petition  and no reason to effectively " punish"  them for wishing to preserve

a piece of La Verne' s history. I urge members  of the Planning Commission to accept the variance pettion  of
Brian and Natalie to retain their carriage house/ single car garage.

Thank you for your attention  to this matter.

Sincerely,
